transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, um… I’m here because things have gotten really bad at work. I’m a barber, and I’ve gotten to the point where I’ll do almost anything to avoid using the straight razor. Like, if a client needs a shave or a lineup where I’d normally use it, I’ll try to switch with someone else, or I’ll make an excuse and say the blade’s missing, or I’ll kind of tuck it away in the drawer so I don’t have to deal with it.

And if I can’t get out of it, if I actually have to use it, I’m just… I’m shaking through the whole shave. It’s embarrassing, and it’s starting to interfere with my work a lot.
Is this fear of using the straight razor something that also happens outside of work, or does it only come up when you're on the job?

It’s mostly at work because that’s where the straight razor is, you know, actually open and in my hand or sitting there at my station. But it’s not like I’m scared of every tool or sharp thing all the time. I can use clippers all day, scissors too, and I know—logically—I know the straight razor is just a tool I trained with. I’ve used it before. It’s part of the job.

But when it’s sitting there open on the counter, especially if I know I’m supposed to use it on someone’s neck or around their hairline, it just feels… wrong. Like this sudden feeling that I’m about to hurt the person, or that I’m going to slip and cut myself badly. Even if nothing is actually happening, just seeing it open makes my stomach drop. So yeah, it comes up around the razor specifically, mostly in the barber shop setting.

Do you ever experience similar feelings of anxiety or avoidance with other tools or situations at work or elsewhere, or is this something that only happens when you’re dealing with the straight razor?

It’s really specifically the straight razor. Like, I don’t have that same reaction with the clippers, even though they’re loud and they’re right up near someone’s skin, and I use scissors all day without thinking twice about it. I can do fades, trims, all of that—normal barber stuff—and I’m fine.

But when that straight razor is sitting open at my station, it’s like my brain just changes the whole situation. I know it’s just a tool, and I know I trained with it, and part of me is aware that I’ve used it before without anything terrible happening. But in the moment it doesn’t feel like that. It feels like I’m about to hurt somebody, like I’m going to slip on their neck or around their hairline, or I’m going to cut myself badly. It’s not really other tools or situations so much as that exact thing—the open blade being there and me needing to use it.
Have you ever had similar intense reactions of anxiety or avoidance in other specific situations, even if they weren’t related to the straight razor?

Um… I’m trying to think. Not really, not that I can point to in the same way. Like, I get nervous about normal life stuff sometimes, sure, but I don’t think I have another situation where I react that strongly or go out of my way to avoid it like this.

With the razor it feels very specific and very immediate—like the second it’s open and I know I’m expected to use it, my body kind of reacts before I can talk myself down. I can’t really think of another object or situation that does that to me. I mean, unless I’m missing something, it’s pretty much just this.
When you're faced with having to use the straight razor, do you experience symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or a feeling of intense dread?

Yeah… yeah, I do. It happens really fast, almost before I’ve even had time to think about it. Like if a client says they want the razor shave, or even just when I flip the blade open and see it there, my chest tightens right away.

And my hands get sweaty, which is honestly one of the worst parts because then I start noticing my hands, and I’m thinking, “Great, now I’m nervous and my hands don’t feel steady,” and that makes the whole thing feel even more dangerous. It’s like my body wants to step back from the chair or put the razor down before I’ve made any kind of decision.

The dread is probably the biggest thing, though. It’s not just mild nerves. It’s this sudden, heavy feeling like something bad is about to happen, even if nothing has happened yet. I can know logically that I’m trained and that I’ve done it before, but in that moment my body reacts like I shouldn’t be anywhere near it.

When you’re not at work or not actually using the straight razor, do you find yourself worrying or thinking a lot about using it—like anticipating the next time you’ll have to use it, or feeling anxious even when it’s not right in front of you?

I don’t know… I mean, not in a constant way, I guess. It’s not like I’m sitting at home all night every night thinking about the razor or anything like that. When I’m away from the shop, I can usually be distracted by normal stuff, and it’s not right there in front of me.

But I think if I know I have a client coming in who might want that kind of shave, or if I’m thinking about my schedule for the next day, then yeah, it can kind of come into my mind. I’ll start thinking, “What if they ask for the razor?” or “What if I can’t get around it this time?” And then I’ll sort of rehearse ways to avoid it or hope they don’t ask. So it’s not like the same immediate panic as when I’m actually holding it, but there’s definitely some anticipation around it.

I guess I’d say the real anxiety hits when it’s about to happen, but the worrying can start before that if I know there’s a chance I’ll have to use it.
When you’re away from work or not near the straight razor, do you find yourself having intrusive thoughts or strong worries about using it, even if it’s not happening right then?

I’m not totally sure I’d call them intrusive thoughts, if I’m understanding that right. Like, I don’t usually have random images or thoughts about it just breaking into my head out of nowhere when I’m completely away from work.

It’s more tied to whether there’s some reason to think about it. If I’m at home making dinner or watching something, I’m usually not sitting there thinking about the straight razor. But if I know I’m working the next day, or I start mentally going through appointments, then it can come up like, “What if someone wants that?” And then I’ll kind of get stuck on that for a bit.

So… strong worries, yes, sometimes, but mostly when there’s a chance I might have to deal with it soon. Not just all the time out of nowhere.
Have you ever avoided places, people, or situations where you thought the straight razor might be present, even if you weren’t at work?

Not really outside of work, no… or at least not in the same way. I don’t usually run into straight razors in normal places, so I’m not avoiding, like, people’s houses or stores because I think one might be there.

It’s really centered around the shop. That’s where it gets bad. I mean, honestly, that’s why I’m here, because I’ve gotten to the point where I’ll do almost anything to not have to use it at work. I’ll try to switch clients with someone else if I think they’re going to ask for a razor shave. I’ve said the blade was missing, or that I needed to grab a fresh one and then kind of steered them toward clippers or something else. I’ve even put the razor away in a drawer where it’s not visible, almost like if I don’t see it, maybe it won’t come up.

And if I can’t get out of it, if I’m stuck and I have to do the shave, I’m just… I’m barely getting through it. I’m shaking through the whole thing and trying to hide it, which makes me even more focused on not messing up. So outside of work, no, I don’t think I’m avoiding many situations because of it, but at work I’m avoiding it constantly.
Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that came out of nowhere, even when there wasn’t anything specific triggering them?

No, I don’t think so… not out of nowhere like that.

I mean, I definitely get really worked up in certain moments, but there’s usually something connected to it. Like, I can point to why it’s happening, even if it feels bigger than it should. I don’t usually just be sitting on the couch or walking around somewhere and suddenly get hit with panic for no reason.

Sometimes I’ll feel on edge if I know something is coming up, or if I’m already thinking about it, but that still feels different from it coming out of nowhere. So… yeah, I don’t think I’ve had those sudden random panic episodes without a trigger.
